articles.name: Agent Memory Techniques
articles.summary: An educational collection of memory-system notebooks. Technique 30 demonstrates local Python simulations of tiered memory and graph patterns; its source observations are not evidence of production deployment or measured quality.

articles.name: Agent Mesh
articles.summary: Agent Mesh is a project-local coordination event store with derived SQLite views and bounded, verified context retrieval. Its source describes append-only correction; deletion and several privacy lifecycle features are explicitly not implemented. No project benchmark was run.

articles.name: agent-afk
articles.summary: A local coding-agent framework with cross-session memory split between prompt-injected hot notes, an FTS5 SQLite fact archive, and searchable Markdown procedures. Source review documents implementation paths, not measured recall or isolation quality.

articles.name: agent-memory-mcp
articles.summary: A Go MCP server and CLI combining persistent SQLite memory, project-document search, and stewardship tools. This review describes inspected code and official documentation, not measured quality.

articles.name: Agent-MemoryForge
articles.summary: Agent-MemoryForge is a Python memory service and integration SDK for agent applications. Its current documented service uses Markdown files as canonical memory and SQLite full-text search as a derived index; a Gateway provides tenant/workspace authentication and routes customer operations.

articles.name: AgentDatabase
articles.summary: AgentDatabase is a multi-project agent-data repository whose OpenAIDatabase subsystem stores structured personal memories as canonical, sharded JSONL with governed mutations and temporal retrieval. Selected source code was inspected at the verified main head; no system benchmark was run.

articles.name: Agentic Context Engine
articles.summary: Agentic Context Engine is an agent learning framework whose Skillbook keeps readable strategies derived from task feedback. Agents receive Skillbook prompt context, while Reflector and SkillManager components analyze outcomes and mutate the strategy collection.

articles.name: Agentic GraphRAG
articles.summary: A Python framework that joins structured document evidence with task histories and versioned decisions in a graph. This review describes selected code and official documentation, not measured quality.

articles.name: Agentic GraphRAG Blueprint
articles.summary: A FastAPI and React reference implementation that ingests documents into a graph plus vector index and offers local graph-augmented and global community-report search. This source review reports implementation observations, not measured quality or performance.

articles.name: AgenticTrading
articles.summary: A trading-agent research platform whose FinAgent Memory subsystem uses a Neo4j graph behind REST, MCP, and A2A interfaces. This review reports code and documentation observations; no benchmark results were collected.

articles.name: AgentMemory
articles.summary: A local-first TypeScript memory layer for coding agents using Markdown files, with an optional qmd search helper and CLI/MCP interfaces. This is a source review, not a measured evaluation.

articles.name: agentmemory
articles.summary: A local-first persistence server and agent integrations that capture coding activity, store observations and memories, and retrieve scoped context through keyword search with optional vector and graph signals. This review records source observations, not measured quality or performance.

articles.name: AgentMemory for .NET
articles.summary: AgentMemory for .NET is an independent Neo4j-backed .NET memory framework. It stores conversation history, structured long-term knowledge, and reasoning traces, then assembles scoped, time-aware context for agent frameworks and direct callers.

articles.name: agentmemory V4
articles.summary: An async-first Python memory library with a persistent store, hybrid retrieval, a relationship graph, consolidation, and REST and MCP interfaces. This review records selected source and documentation observations; it does not run agentmemory or reproduce upstream benchmark claims.

articles.name: AgentOS
articles.summary: AgentOS is a TypeScript agent framework whose cognitive-memory layer encodes scoped traces, retrieves and assembles context, and can connect memory to working, graph, archive, and SQL-backed stores. This is a source review, not an execution or performance assessment.

articles.name: AgentOS (Tanglies)
articles.summary: AgentOS combines an in-process, bounded session history with SQLite-backed long-term memory. Long-term recall uses weighted keyword matching over English tokens and Chinese character bigrams; this review records source observations and does not execute the service or benchmark.

articles.name: AgentRecall-X
articles.summary: A local-first memory framework and MCP, SDK, and CLI stack organized around persistent project context and a governed correction ledger, with an optional hosted multi-user service. This review records source observations, not measured quality or performance.

articles.name: AgentRT
articles.summary: AgentRT is a C11 agent runtime whose mem_d daemon stores bounded memory records in JSONL, searches by TF-IDF plus substring scoring with optional embeddings, and exposes write, retrieval, deletion, knowledge-base, cache and context-ledger APIs. This is a source review, not a runtime or performance assessment.

articles.name: Agents Remember
articles.summary: Agents Remember gives coding agents a Git-versioned knowledge tree with source-path cards, structured records and a workflow that checks recorded knowledge against code changes. The reviewed source describes repository-scoped memory, a derived read index, Curator-authored updates and bounded path or record reads.

articles.name: agents-memory
articles.summary: agents-memory is a local, Markdown-first memory vault with a Python MCP server and CLI. It separates global user memory from per-repository notes, builds a disposable SQLite FTS5 index for retrieval, and uses staging and explicit distillation to move selected material into typed files. This review is based on selected source and documentation at a verified repository revision; no runtime results were collected.

articles.name: AgentSwarms
articles.summary: AgentSwarms is a self-hosted agent and data platform whose memory subsystem combines conversation summaries and scratchpads with optional per-agent long-term notes. Long-term recall uses indexed keyword overlap; this review records source observations, not benchmark results.

articles.name: AgentWorkingMemory
articles.summary: AgentWorkingMemory (AWM) is a local-first agent memory application with selective writes, multi-stage retrieval, correction and retraction flows, and local or server database backends. This is a source review, not a runtime or performance assessment.

articles.name: Agno
articles.summary: Agno is an agent platform with a typed learning subsystem for user profiles, long-term user memories, session context, entity memory, learned knowledge, and decision logs. The source review describes configurable extraction and tool-mediated updates; it reports no benchmark measurements.

articles.name: Agora
articles.summary: Agora is a self-hosted agent collaboration platform. Its hosted-session subsystem stores an agent-authored final-turn summary and injects it into a later wake when a native CLI session cannot be resumed. The summary is a bounded text fallback, not a searchable fact store.

articles.name: AI Agent Automation
articles.summary: AI Agent Automation is a self-hosted workflow platform with optional per-agent conversation memory. At the reviewed head, memory stores conversation envelopes with embeddings in MongoDB and retrieves them by scanning an agent's conversation rows and ranking cosine similarity in application code. This is a source review, not a benchmark result.

articles.name: AI Agents in Depth
articles.summary: A book repository with chapter companion projects. This review is bounded to its Chapter 3 user-memory example: local JSON-backed notes/cards, separate conversational and background processing, and provider-backed LLM tools. No runtime, benchmark, or tests were run.

articles.name: AI Brain Starter
articles.summary: A local-first Claude Code and Obsidian vault setup whose memory is represented by Markdown notes and an index, with hooks and session workflows for routing, checks, and capture. This review reports inspected sources, not measured outcomes.

articles.name: AI Maestro
articles.summary: AI Maestro is a self-hosted agent orchestration platform with an optional per-agent long-term memory skill. It indexes conversation messages, consolidates selected passages into memory cards and an entity graph, and injects relevant context into later prompts. This is a source review; outcome quality and performance were not measured.

articles.name: AI Workflow Workspace
articles.summary: AI Workflow Workspace is a project-local, agent-agnostic coding workflow with scripts for routing, indexed lookup, task handoff, and persistent Markdown knowledge. This review records source behavior only; no runtime or benchmark results were collected.

articles.name: ai-memory
articles.summary: A self-hosted memory service for coding agents that captures sanitized session observations, compiles them into a git-versioned Markdown wiki, and retrieves project context across agent sessions. SQLite is a derived index; the default capture, search, and handoff paths are designed to work without an LLM provider. This review records source observations, not measured system or benchmark results.

articles.name: AideMemo
articles.summary: AideMemo is a local-first Rust memory library and agent integration toolkit. It stores explicit typed facts connected to entities and relations, supports temporal history and retrieval, and exposes its store through MCP, a CLI, SDKs, and language bindings. This is a source review; outcome quality and performance were not measured.

articles.name: aigent-OS
articles.summary: aigent-OS is a local Claude Code harness with Git-backed Markdown memory, local semantic search, and managed context-refresh capsules. This bounded review combines official README documentation with a narrow current code-diff inspection; it is not a runtime or quality assessment.

articles.name: AIMAOS
articles.summary: AIMAOS is a local-first, single-operator multi-agent office workstation. Its per-agent mRAG stores keep raw conversation chunks and derived categorized beliefs in local JSON files, then inject a bounded selection into the agent prompt. This review records pinned-source observations; no runtime or benchmark measurements were collected.

articles.name: aimee
articles.summary: Aimee is a self-hosted runtime with personal memory on Server and optional shared memory on KB. At the reviewed public revision, memory storage and retrieval are supplied by a private implementation bundle; this review documents the public generic SDK, module boundary, and host controls, not the private datastore or ranking policy.

articles.name: aios (rexleimo)
articles.summary: AIOS is a local-first control plane for coding agents. ContextDB stores project sessions, events, checkpoints and pull-based context; a separate memo plane stores durable, scoped facts. This review describes pinned source and documentation, not runtime quality or performance.

articles.name: AIPass
articles.summary: AIPass is a local agent workspace whose in-tree memory branch keeps agent state in bounded .trinity JSON files and archives older entries into ChromaDB for semantic search across branches.

articles.name: AKB
articles.summary: AKB is an organizational knowledge base for agents with versioned documents, tables, files, relations, and hybrid search through MCP, REST, and a web UI. PostgreSQL is the Native backend's source of truth; pluggable vector indexes are derived retrieval data. This review covers selected pinned source and documentation, not runtime quality or performance.

articles.name: All Agentic Architectures
articles.summary: A Python library and runnable textbook containing multiple agent patterns, including several distinct memory designs. It is not one unified memory product: selected implementations combine vector episodes, graph facts, bounded context/archive tiers, or learned workflow recipes. This source review did not execute the library or evaluate memory quality.

articles.name: ALMA
articles.summary: ALMA is a local-first agent memory and learning library with typed records for outcomes, heuristics, anti-patterns, domain knowledge, and user preferences. Its Python retrieval engine combines embedding search, configurable scoring, optional feedback reranking, and caching over selectable storage backends. This review describes selected sources at the pinned head and reports no ALMA measurements.

articles.name: AlphaOne ai-memory
articles.summary: A self-hosted Rust agent-memory library and daemon with MCP, HTTP, and CLI surfaces, using SQLite or PostgreSQL plus Apache AGE and optional vector retrieval. This is a bounded source review, not a runtime evaluation.

articles.name: ALTK-Evolve
articles.summary: ALTK-Evolve learns reusable guidelines from agent trajectories, stores entities in a selectable backend, and retrieves a task-specific set for later sessions. This is a bounded source review; no runtime or benchmark was run.

articles.name: Always-On Memory Agent
articles.summary: A Google ADK sample that uses a local SQLite store, background file ingestion and consolidation, and an aiohttp query API. This bounded source review does not measure runtime behavior.

articles.name: AMITY / Archangel-8
articles.summary: AMITY is a local Python session-memory and CovenantVault implementation paired with a C++ sensory/orchestration layer and optional ZeroMQ IPC. The curated repository locator currently returns 404; this review uses the same-owner public Amity-v2.0 repository as the current AMITY candidate and records lineage as unresolved.

articles.name: anatid
articles.summary: anatid is an embedded Python memory library using a DuckDB file for versioned facts, entities, relationships, and source episodes. It combines temporal SQL visibility with graph, BM25, and optional vector retrieval. This review describes selected documentation and code at the pinned head; it did not run anatid or its benchmarks.

articles.name: Anda Brain
articles.summary: Anda Brain is a self-hosted memory service for agents. Formation turns interactions into a versioned knowledge graph, Recall answers from that graph, and Maintenance consolidates and reviews it. This review reports current source and documentation observations, not benchmark measurements.

articles.name: Anda DB
articles.summary: Anda DB is an embedded Rust document database and workspace of storage, retrieval, and KIP components for persistent agent memory. The Cognitive Nexus models concepts, claims, evidence, and activity, with belief projected from assertions at read time. This is a pinned source review, not a runtime or benchmark evaluation.

articles.name: Animus
articles.summary: Animus is a self-hosted C++ agent framework whose memory spans per-agent episodic observations, semantic ontology, raw memory files, and a unified search/context path. The inspected source exposes mutations and retrieval structures; no runtime quality or performance was measured.

articles.name: ANOLISA Agent Memory
articles.summary: ANOLISA Agent Memory is a Linux-oriented, file-first memory component served to agents through MCP. Markdown files are the durable store; an optional SQLite search index supplies keyword and embedding retrieval, while tools support observation, context assembly, snapshots, and user-controlled forgetting. This review is pinned source inspection, not a runtime or benchmark result.

articles.name: AnythingLLM
articles.summary: AnythingLLM is a self-hostable AI application with a first-party relational memory path. The reviewed implementation stores user-global and user-workspace facts and injects bounded memory text into chat prompts; source-level behavior is described separately from unmeasured outcomes.

articles.name: AnythingMCP
articles.summary: AnythingMCP is a self-hosted MCP gateway with workspace memory for facts, preferences, and notes. Its memory service stores personal and organization items in PostgreSQL, offers scoped full-text search, and connects entity-tagged memory to a workspace knowledge graph.

articles.name: AOCI-CODE
articles.summary: AOCI-CODE is a local Go CLI and stdio MCP server that helps a coding agent maintain a Git-versioned, plain-text map of a repository. Its current Cognition Volumes workflow serves selected index contents, validates model-authored updates against repository state, and publishes formal index changes through guarded transactions; this review did not measure runtime quality or performance.

articles.name: Apache Maka
articles.summary: Apache Maka is an Apache incubating, local-first agent workspace. Its memory behavior has two complementary parts: a revisioned personal/project fact store with evidence and explicit edits, and a searchable, indexed record of authorized conversation history. The project is a full agent workspace, not a standalone memory library.

articles.name: arc-code
articles.summary: A general-purpose coding-agent harness for playing ARC-AGI-3 through a small actuator. It makes a generated action log the agent's complete game memory, while the agent can create notes and helper programs in a per-game workspace. A broker, isolated sandbox, audit trail, and optional Postgres record support controlled and reviewable runs. This article records source observations at the pinned revision; no system or benchmark was run.

articles.name: archeus
articles.summary: Archeus is a local workspace and memory layer for coding agents. It builds a per-project semantic graph from repository files and session transcripts, then exposes compact project memory through a launcher digest, path-scoped rules, and optional prompt-time retrieval. A separate lesson pipeline extracts durable decisions and corrections from sessions.

articles.name: Archiver RAG
articles.summary: Archiver RAG is a local memory layer built around an Obsidian Markdown vault, a persistent Chroma vector index, a file watcher, and MCP tools for search and vault operations. This is a pinned source review, not a runtime or benchmark evaluation.

articles.name: Arcon
articles.summary: Arcon is a local-first digital companion application with a modular TypeScript memory subsystem. The reviewed package combines SQLite records, extraction and review, lifecycle and scope filters, lexical ranking, entity knowledge, and reflection proposals. This is a pinned source review; no runtime or benchmark results were produced.

articles.name: ArcRift
articles.summary: ArcRift is a local-first AI memory application combining a browser extension, desktop dashboard, backend, and MCP server. It stores conversations and extracted graph facts by project/session, then retrieves vector, keyword, and graph context for browser prompts or coding agents. This pinned source review contains no runtime or benchmark results.

articles.name: Areev
articles.summary: Areev is an embedded Rust memory engine and Open Memory Spec implementation. It stores typed, immutable, content-addressed memory grains in per-memory database files, queries them through CAL, and can assemble budgeted context. Areev Loop adds optional review-gated improvement workflows. This review reports selected source and documentation observations, not runtime measurements.

articles.name: ARGO
articles.summary: ARGO is a repository-centered software delivery framework that uses an ArchiMate knowledge graph as durable project context. A canonical JSON architecture document is validated and read through MCP; Neo4j and its vector indexes act as derived semantic projections for query and context assembly. This is a pinned source review, not an execution or benchmark assessment.

articles.name: Artesian
articles.summary: Artesian is a Rust memory and context-control system for agents. Its aquifer crate provides durable memory backends and retrieval; the optional headgate layer qualifies what enters a bounded working context. This review describes pinned source and documentation, not runtime behavior.

articles.name: ARTEX
articles.summary: ARTEX is a self-hosted, LLM-driven penetration-testing application whose persistent memory includes a shared asset graph, per-task exploration graphs, activity traces, and an optional evidence-gated lesson library. Source inspection shows how these records are written, selected, and framed for agents; no ARTEX runtime or benchmark was run.

articles.name: Atomic Agent
articles.summary: Atomic Agent is a local-first agent whose durable memory lives outside the chat transcript in a versioned SQLite database. It combines profile facts, searchable notes, links, lessons, and procedures, then injects bounded selected context into prompts. This review describes pinned source and documentation; it does not report a runtime or benchmark result.

articles.name: Attune AI
articles.summary: Attune AI combines cross-session findings, curated project lessons, and prompt-triggered lesson recall. Its inspected design uses expiring raw findings, human-gated promotion, local files, and an optional Redis memory backend; this review contains no new measurements.

articles.name: Aukora Kernel
articles.summary: Aukora Kernel is an authority-and-receipt framework, not a standalone memory database. At the reviewed repository head, memory behavior sits in broader Symbiote host/reference layers: a local IDE JSONL store and an internal Convex memory path. The portable @aukora/kernel verifier/reducer has no persistence capability. This review records source observations only; no runtime or benchmark results were produced.

articles.name: Aura
articles.summary: Aura is a local desktop assistant whose memory subsystem combines working context, SQLite episodic records, semantic/vector stores, entity and knowledge graphs, procedural memory, and retention/consolidation paths. This review describes selected current source at a pinned commit; it does not measure runtime quality.

articles.name: Aura (chetto1983)
articles.summary: Aura is a self-hosted Go agent platform whose memory subsystem stores bitemporal facts as graph edges in ArcadeDB, alongside derived conversation recall. It combines named-entity traversal with hybrid lexical and vector retrieval, and exposes correction, forgetting, and provenance-aware writes. This is a pinned source review; no runtime or benchmark results were produced.

articles.name: AuraOS
articles.summary: AuraOS is a small Flask chat application that combines local identity text and a per-user transcript into prompts sent to Ollama. The inspected route reads the entire transcript and appends each successful exchange; no workload results were measured.

articles.name: AURORA
articles.summary: AURORA is a local code-aware memory and intelligence layer for coding assistants. The official repository is archived; this review inspected selected documentation and core storage code at the verified main head and ran no system or benchmark.

articles.name: Auto Company
articles.summary: Auto Company is a self-hosted continuous-work framework for coding assistants. Each fresh CLI cycle receives a shared Markdown consensus file, performs work under project prompts and rules, and rewrites that file as the handoff for the next cycle. This is a pinned source review, not a runtime or benchmark evaluation.

articles.name: AutoBot
articles.summary: AutoBot is a self-hosted AI platform whose memory is split across general SQLite memory, durable PostgreSQL knowledge facts and their Redis/vector projections, a Redis-backed graph, and conversation-derived trajectory and verbatim stores. This is a pinned source review, not a runtime or benchmark evaluation.

articles.name: AutoGen
articles.summary: AutoGen is a multi-agent application framework with a pluggable Python memory interface. Its common contract stores and retrieves MemoryContent, while implementations choose persistence, ranking, and context injection. This is a source review; no workload results were measured.

articles.name: autoharness
articles.summary: autoharness is a Claude Code plugin that learns and maintains native skill folders from work in a session. It captures bounded, redacted session evidence, asks a reflector to propose changes, and uses a deterministic promoter to validate and write them. The project records use-related signals for recall and lifecycle management; this is a pinned source review, not a runtime or benchmark evaluation.

articles.name: AutoMem
articles.summary: A self-hostable memory API for AI assistants that pairs a FalkorDB graph as its canonical record with Qdrant vectors for semantic retrieval, exposed through REST and MCP integrations. This review reports pinned source and documentation observations; it does not measure runtime quality or performance.

articles.name: AutoResearchClaw
articles.summary: AutoResearchClaw is a research-paper pipeline with a local JSONL memory library, a separate run-scoped lesson store, and an optional lesson-to-skill bridge. The review reports source observations only; the system and benchmarks were not run.

articles.name: Backboard Desktop
articles.summary: Backboard Desktop is an open-source desktop agent IDE. Its README advertises memory across chats, while the bounded current CLI source inspection found durable per-session conversation and request logs but no semantic memory store or cross-chat recall path. This review records source observations and does not establish runtime memory behavior.

articles.name: basemode
articles.summary: A local Rust CLI and Claude Code hook integration that stores project, decision, note, rule, document, and code-structure knowledge in an RDF graph and injects selected context at relevant events. This source review is not a benchmark or runtime assessment.

articles.name: Basic Memory
articles.summary: Basic Memory is a local-first knowledge management system in which Markdown notes are the durable source of truth and an indexed database provides structured graph, full-text, and optional semantic retrieval. Humans and MCP clients can read and update the same notes; local and hosted deployments share the note model while using different storage and routing adapters.

articles.name: beads
articles.summary: Beads is a Dolt-backed, workspace-scoped task graph for coding agents that also exposes a small persistent memory plane. Named memories are stored as string values in a reserved namespace, can be recalled or forgotten by exact key, and are appended to `bd prime` session context. This is a pinned source review, not a runtime or benchmark evaluation.

articles.name: Beever Atlas
articles.summary: Beever Atlas distills team conversations into channel-scoped facts and graph relationships, then serves them through hybrid retrieval, a cited Q&A agent, a maintained wiki, and MCP. The review records source observations only; no runtime or benchmark results were measured.

articles.name: Beevibe
articles.summary: Beevibe is a self-hosted team workspace whose memory combines stable per-agent prompt blocks with vector-searchable archival facts in Postgres/pgvector. This review describes selected code at a verified repository revision; it does not run the service or measure memory quality or performance.

articles.name: Bifrost
articles.summary: Bifrost is a Rust/Axum agent runtime with a small Memvid-backed conversation memory path. The inspected implementation appends each turn as a frame and exposes a search tool; this review records source observations, not measured quality or performance.

articles.name: billion-context
articles.summary: billion-context is a context-compression proxy and host plugin. It lets agents fold conversation ranges into summaries, then search or restore the retained history by session and message references.

articles.name: Binder
articles.summary: Binder is a local-first structured knowledge base for records, configuration, and relations, backed by workspace-local SQLite and hash-linked transactions. This is a source review, not a runtime or benchmark evaluation.

articles.name: BitterBot Desktop
articles.summary: Bitterbot Desktop is a local-first personal agent whose memory combines searchable conversation and file chunks, canonical facts, and a knowledge graph in SQLite. This review describes selected source and official documentation at a verified upstream revision; it does not run the application or measure retrieval quality or performance.

articles.name: Bolt PCHIE
articles.summary: Bolt PCHIE is a deterministic robotics research harness whose Little Nemo agent can record episodic maze runs and optionally use prior outcomes to adjust search. The reviewed memory paths are small bounded ledgers with integrity checks; they are not general-purpose conversational memory.

articles.name: Bot Board
articles.summary: Bot Board is a self-hosted collaboration board for coding agents. Its workspace knowledge base stores path-addressed Markdown documents as append-only revisions with author, reason, and source strings; agents retrieve them through API paths and channel references. This review describes source behavior at the verified GitHub mirror head and includes no runtime or benchmark result.

articles.name: Brain
articles.summary: Brain is a pre-release Rust memory database with a binary wire protocol. It stores raw experiences alongside typed entities, claims, and relations, and combines semantic, lexical, and graph retrieval. This review records source observations, not measured system or benchmark results.

articles.name: brain-mcp
articles.summary: brain-mcp is a local transcript recorder and MCP server that keeps an append-only byte floor with a re-derivable DuckDB BM25 index, returning line-and-hash citations or a scoped abstention. Source review only; no runtime or benchmark results were measured.

articles.name: brain.md
articles.summary: brain.md is a repository-native memory toolkit for coding agents. It uses Markdown files plus a small Node.js CLI to store durable project knowledge, with explicit commands for reading, writing, revising, indexing, and archiving pages.

articles.name: BrainAPI
articles.summary: BrainAPI is a Python service that turns ingested material into an event-centered knowledge graph and exposes graph, passage, and typed-fact retrieval. This review distinguishes README design descriptions and selected current code paths from unmeasured behavior.

articles.name: breadcrumbs
articles.summary: Breadcrumbs is a public repository of coding-agent memory templates, hooks, scripts, and guardrails, rather than a hosted memory service. It places cues at session start, prompt lookup, file edits, and handoff, and includes two distinct file-backed examples: a TSV-indexed memory desk and a separate Python three-tier memory engine. This is source review, not runtime or benchmark evidence.

articles.name: Brigade
articles.summary: BrigadeStack is an agent-workspace CLI with repository Markdown cards, ingested handoff proposals, deterministic BM25 search, bounded session-start recall, and optional hub synchronization. A distinct optional Obsidian vault module indexes configured roots and stages additive proposals. This is a source review, not a runtime or performance assessment.

articles.name: Browsentic
articles.summary: Browsentic is a local browser-agent harness with separate persistent context paths for a user profile, site-specific notes or generated maps, and recorded browsing workflows. This review examines selected source at a verified revision and does not run the application or measure memory quality or performance.

articles.name: Buzz
articles.summary: Buzz is a self-hostable collaboration workspace whose agent-memory slice is NIP-AE: encrypted per-agent/owner engrams, a memory CLI, and ACP session-time core-profile injection. This is a pinned source review, not a runtime or benchmark result.

articles.name: ByteChef
articles.summary: ByteChef combines workflow-integrated chat-memory backends with a document knowledge base. The reviewed knowledge-base path loads, chunks, embeds and retrieves documents through a shared pgvector vector store, with metadata filters and knowledge-base scoping. This is a source review, not a runtime or benchmark measurement.

articles.name: ByteRover
articles.summary: ByteRover CLI (brv) is a project knowledge and agent memory toolkit. Its main project-memory path curates structured HTML or Markdown topics under a project context tree and retrieves them with a cached local BM25 index; a separate Cipher MemoryManager stores scratch memories as blobs.

articles.name: Cairn
articles.summary: Cairn is a server and dispatcher for goal-directed exploration. It stores project knowledge as a graph of facts and intents, with hints as separate project annotations, then gives worker agents the project state to explore. This review reports source observations only; no Cairn workload or benchmark was run.

articles.name: Cambium
articles.summary: Cambium is a governance standard and reference toolset for LLM-maintained knowledge repositories. It provides policies, controlled mutation tools, evidence ledgers, recovery state, and agent-host interfaces; adopters own the corpus and selected profile. This is a source review, not a benchmark.

articles.name: Elastic Atlas
articles.summary: Elastic Atlas is a research demo and agent memory layer on Elasticsearch. It stores episodic events, semantic facts, and procedural playbooks in separate indices and offers user-scoped hybrid retrieval with optional catalog federation. Source review describes implementation paths and limits; no system, tests, or benchmarks were run.

articles.name: Elephantasm
articles.summary: A Python framework that transforms agent interaction events into curated memories, typed knowledge, identity, and token-budgeted prompt packs. This review records code evidence at one verified revision; no system behavior or performance was measured.

articles.name: ELIOT Memory OS
articles.summary: ELIOT Memory OS currently publishes a V3 design baseline for a local-first memory daemon, provenance-aware revisions, scoped retrieval, and controlled erasure. Upstream says V3 is not a released runtime and its Store candidate is unqualified; this review reports design contracts, not verified behavior or benchmark results.

articles.name: elizaOS
articles.summary: A TypeScript/VibeLang agent framework whose current core defines scoped message and long-term memory types, ranked retrieval, adapter-owned persistence, and source-aware embedding writes. The current branch is a specification-led rewrite; runtime conformance and performance were not measured.

articles.name: eMEM
articles.summary: eMEM is an embedded Python memory library for embodied agents. It combines SQLite graph records, HNSW, FTS5, and spatial indexing for semantic and spatiotemporal retrieval. The public API has no explicit memory edit or delete operation, and the reviewed library does not implement tenant isolation. Runtime quality and performance were not measured.

articles.name: emem (Vortx AI)
articles.summary: emem is a Rust protocol and service for addressable signed facts and shared agent notes. It uses content identifiers, receipts, and a transparency log; notes are public and deletion unpublishes rather than erases their retained bytes. No system behavior or performance was measured for this review.

articles.name: Empirica
articles.summary: Empirica is a local-first Python CLI and library for recording and evaluating an agent’s work beliefs, evidence, and outcomes. It uses SQLite for project records, Git notes for versioned history, and optional Qdrant for semantic retrieval. The three stores have different roles and can diverge; no runtime quality or performance was measured.

articles.name: Empryo
articles.summary: Empryo is an agent coding harness whose public SoulForge v2 core includes persistent cross-session memory. The inspected memory subsystem stores categorized records in separate project and global SQLite databases, combines lexical, semantic, file and usage signals for recall, and supports updates, restorable soft deletion, and supersession. The repository says the public source is not the full current Empryo v3 source; runtime quality and performance were not measured.

articles.name: Emulo
articles.summary: Emulo mines user-authored coding-agent session logs into dated, quote-backed Markdown instruction profiles. It provides a local extractor and a plugin/bootstrap workflow with report validation and versioned profile activation. Retrieval loads whole domain profiles rather than performing ranked memory search; runtime quality and efficiency were not measured.

articles.name: Engram
articles.summary: Engram is a local-first Go memory system for coding agents, exposing MCP, HTTP, CLI, and TUI interfaces over SQLite + FTS5. Optional Git export and cloud replication support sharing. This review describes pinned source and documentation; runtime quality and performance were not measured.

articles.name: engram (NickCirv)
articles.summary: Engram is a local code graph and context tool for coding agents. It indexes source entities and relationships, selected Git and session information, and optional skills into project-local SQLite, then exposes graph retrieval through CLI, hooks, MCP, and a local authenticated HTTP interface.

articles.name: Engram Alpha
articles.summary: Engram Alpha is a local-first graph memory for software projects, exposed through an MCP and HTTP core, CLI, IDE extensions, and a web pane. It stores typed nodes and relations in one graph file per project, then serves hybrid keyword/vector retrieval with graph context, trust and confidence signals. This review is source-based; no runtime or benchmark was executed.

articles.name: Engram Cognitive
articles.summary: Engram Cognitive is a local-first Python memory library that stores episodic observations, extracted semantic facts, and graph relationships in one SQLite file, with optional vector, LLM, MCP, and event integrations.

articles.name: Engram Format
articles.summary: Engram Format is the open Rust crate and specification for an encrypted SQLite vault and encrypted sync wire format used by the closed-source Engram product. The inspected crate includes capture and retrieval helpers, embeddings, a write-through associative cache, and sync data types; this review does not measure product behavior or performance.

articles.name: Engram MCP (edg-l)
articles.summary: Engram MCP is a local Rust MCP server and CLI for coding-agent memory. It stores typed memories, branch-linked handoffs, todos, and ADRs in SQLite, with local ONNX embeddings and FTS5 hybrid retrieval. Scope is project and branch aware, with optional cross-project global memories. This is a source review; no runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run.

articles.name: Engram Provable
articles.summary: Engram is a Go memory service for AI agents with HTTP and MCP interfaces and PostgreSQL/pgvector storage. It models semantic beliefs with episodic, procedural and working memory, tenant and subject bindings, hybrid recall, and provenance/audit features. This is a source review; no runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run.

articles.name: Engraphis
articles.summary: Engraphis is a local-first memory system for coding agents. Its source describes a scoped SQLite store with temporal history, graph and vector retrieval, lexical search, and MCP or dashboard interfaces. This review records source behavior only; no local benchmark or runtime result was produced.

articles.name: enquire-mcp
articles.summary: enquire-mcp is a local-first MCP server and CLI that makes an Obsidian-format vault searchable by multiple agents. It combines lexical, TF-IDF, embedding, and optional reranking paths, and exposes note paths, excerpts, freshness metadata, and PDF page citations. This is a bounded source review; no system measurements were collected.

articles.name: EverOS
articles.summary: EverOS is a local-first Python memory runtime that keeps canonical memory in Markdown and uses SQLite plus a derived LanceDB index for retrieval. Writes and derived processing are asynchronous at different stages, so stored and searchable state can temporarily diverge.

articles.name: EvoMemNav
articles.summary: EvoMemNav is a training-free embodied navigation agent. It builds a visual-semantic graph of observed views and objects and uses episode-local verification feedback plus per-scene JSON experience memory to rank candidate views and guide later decisions. This is a source review; the system, tests, and benchmarks were not run.

articles.name: EvoX Genesis
articles.summary: EvoX Genesis is an open-source software-development agent system that supplies project context from repository-local Markdown files scoped to an agent's repository path. Git versions project changes and SQLite stores runtime/task data; product behavior and performance were not measured.

articles.name: Exomem
articles.summary: The current project describes a local-first memory server for agent clients that reads and writes a user's Markdown/Obsidian vault through MCP, CLI, and REST interfaces. Its design separates captured Sources, authored knowledge pages, and Evidence; retrieval combines lexical, semantic, and graph-related paths. This review is limited to public source and documentation, not runtime behavior.

articles.name: FARM
articles.summary: A robotics scene-memory framework that maps RGB-D streams into an object-level 3D memory and retrieves objects from natural-language descriptions and spatial relations. This review records source observations, not measured quality or performance.

articles.name: FAVA Trails
articles.summary: FAVA Trails is an MCP memory server for reviewed agent decisions and observations. It stores Markdown thought records in a separate Jujutsu/Git data repository, gates shared recall on approval, and uses lexical substring matching; this source review collected no runtime or benchmark measurements.

articles.name: feltstate
articles.summary: Feltstate is a local Python reference library that pairs a structured, decaying fact store with optional provenance, lifecycle, and affect mechanisms. This source review records implementation observations, not measured quality or performance.

articles.name: FERNme
articles.summary: FERNme is a user-personalization memory library with a deterministic weighted graph and event log, SQLite or Postgres stores, REST and MCP interfaces, and optional semantic search and proposal enrichment. The review records source observations only; no local benchmark or runtime result was produced.

articles.name: Fidelis Memory
articles.summary: Fidelis Memory is a local-first Python memory service for coding agents. It stores original passages in a local Chroma vector store, uses configured Ollama embeddings, and exposes bounded retrieval through HTTP and MCP. Its current documented MCP surface supports storage, correction and reads but no record deletion. This review describes source and documentation; runtime quality and resource use were not measured.

articles.name: Fireweed MCP
articles.summary: A local MCP memory server that stores structured claims only after deterministic checks compare each proposed claim with quoted evidence. It returns grounded records with byte-range receipts and abstains on many ungrounded queries; its README describes retrieval recall as a major limitation.

articles.name: Flair
articles.summary: Flair is a self-hosted agent identity and memory service built as a native Harper application. It stores agent memories in Harper/RocksDB, creates embeddings in process, and combines vector and lexical retrieval. This is a source-based review; no system behavior or performance was measured.

articles.name: Flatbread Proof
articles.summary: Flatbread Proof is a Git-tracked project-memory graph in the Flatbread monorepo. It stores typed Markdown records under an Effort and provides a CLI for bounded reads and validated lifecycle mutations. This review is based on current documentation and source; runtime behavior and performance were not measured.

articles.name: flow
articles.summary: flow is a local CLI for tracking work across agent sessions. It keeps task and project metadata in SQLite and briefs, progress notes, and a small shared knowledge base as Markdown files. Retrieval is directed through task context and agent file reads rather than a dedicated memory search engine. This is a source review; no system behavior or performance was measured.

articles.name: Flowix
articles.summary: Flowix is an agent-workspace application whose local MCP/CLI interface lets agents search and manage Markdown notes and structured collections inside configured notebooks. Markdown files are canonical note content, with a rebuildable SQLite projection for indexed access.

articles.name: Flowly
articles.summary: Flowly is a self-hosted personal agent with a layered memory system: workspace Markdown notes, a SQLite-backed chunk search index, a temporal knowledge graph, and a separate SQLite governance store for confidence, privacy, lifecycle and audit metadata. The reviewed code combines keyword retrieval with optional embeddings and background consolidation; these source observations do not establish retrieval quality or isolation.

articles.name: FluctlightDB
articles.summary: FluctlightDB is a Rust memory engine with Python and HTTP interfaces. It stores episodic memories as Episodes inside neural Engrams and recalls them from cues through a hybrid index and graph activation path. A brain is persisted in a local brain directory or legacy file; multi-agent/server setups add per-agent or per-tenant storage and access configuration.

articles.name: Forgetful
articles.summary: Forgetful is a self-hostable MCP memory and knowledge service with SQLite or PostgreSQL storage, semantic search, optional reranking and keyword fusion, and an agent-facing CLI and HTTP API.

articles.name: Friday
articles.summary: Friday is a Python memory service for coding agents. Its Compose gateway combines a JSON facts ledger, Mem0-backed episodic search, Neo4j graph extraction, and lifecycle processing; an opt-in gateway uses project-keyed SQLite/libSQL and FTS5. This review covers source behavior only; no runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run.

articles.name: funes
articles.summary: funes indexes coding-agent sessions into a local Lance vector dataset and recalls passages with hybrid search and reranking. Optional Hugging Face dataset publishing shares an append-oriented memory across agents and machines.

articles.name: fx
articles.summary: Current fx is a native Zig coding agent whose persistent memory is primarily its resumable conversation history. It stores session events locally, compacts older turns to fit model context, and keeps originals available for later lookup. This review did not find a separate durable fact store or run the system.

articles.name: gaius
articles.summary: A self-hosted memory lifecycle manager for coding agents. It extracts and records facts into a local SQLite corpus, ranks facts for injection and search, and supports review, decay, and optional semantic retrieval.

articles.name: Gas Town
articles.summary: Gas Town is a multi-agent workspace manager. Its memory feature stores typed text values through the Beads key-value interface and injects them into agent context at prime time; retrieval is a full listing rather than relevance-ranked recall.

articles.name: GBrain
articles.summary: GBrain is a self-hostable memory service and agent integration around canonical Markdown pages, a Postgres-compatible database engine, hybrid search, graph retrieval, optional synthesis, and background maintenance. These documented features are not measured quality results.

articles.name: Generative Agents
articles.summary: Generative Agents is a research simulation whose personas keep JSON-backed associative memory streams of events, chats, and derived thoughts. Perception appends observations, retrieval ranks event/thought nodes, and reflection stores thoughts with supporting node IDs. This review describes inspected source, not measured memory quality or performance.

articles.name: GenericAgent
articles.summary: GenericAgent is a local autonomous-agent framework whose memory is a prompt-guided hierarchy of text files: an index, global facts, reusable task skills, and archived session records. This source review does not measure recall, isolation, cost, or runtime performance.

articles.name: GENOME
articles.summary: GENOME is a Python memory library with SQLite or PostgreSQL storage, local embeddings by default, optional fact extraction and conflict resolution, scoped retrieval, temporal entity facts, and MCP/REST interfaces. Its source includes provenance quarantine and an opt-in mutation journal; this review did not run the system or measure it.

articles.name: gh-aw
articles.summary: GitHub Agentic Workflows (gh-aw) compiles Markdown workflow definitions into GitHub Actions workflows and offers file-backed memory through Actions cache, Git branches, and an experimental GitHub Drives preview.

articles.name: Gini Agent
articles.summary: Gini Agent's Hindsight memory subsystem stores structured units in per-instance SQLite and retrieves them through semantic, lexical, graph, and temporal channels. This is a source review, not a measured quality result.

articles.name: GitLord
articles.summary: A Python agent-orchestration framework that stores turns and tool events as Git commits, with session and subagent branches plus JSON and optional vector indexes. This review records source observations, not measured quality or performance.

articles.name: GitMem
articles.summary: GitMem is an MCP server for retaining coding-agent lessons such as scars, wins, patterns, decisions, and threads across sessions. The free path stores JSON locally and searches lexically; the opt-in Pro/dev path uses Supabase and supports vector recall. This is a source review, not a measured quality or security result.

articles.name: Global Agent Memory
articles.summary: Global Agent Memory is a local-first memory MCP service and companion CLI/dashboard. It stores canonical notes as Markdown in an Obsidian-compatible Vault, with a rebuildable SQLite index for keyword and optional semantic retrieval. It supports project-aware context, reviewable candidate memories, and owner-controlled visibility and access. These are source and documentation observations, not quality or isolation measurements.

articles.name: GMEOW
articles.summary: GMEOW is a Rust-first ontology and MCP project whose grounded-memory tools store attributed, revisable claims in a portable GTS ai-package. The documented triad supports explicit claim writes, recall, and suppression-based belief revision; this review did not run the software or measure retrieval quality or efficiency.

articles.name: GMR
articles.summary: GMR (Grounded Memory Runtime) is a Rust runtime that connects externally stored memories and one-shot conclusions to versioned observations of facts they depend on. It surfaces memories when their declared grounding changes and reports whether conclusions still stand; it is an anchoring and provenance layer, not a semantic memory store or a judge of claim truth.

articles.name: Gobii
articles.summary: Gobii is an always-on agent platform whose memory behavior combines agent-authored tables in per-agent SQLite databases with summarized communications and execution history. This review is pinned to current upstream source; it does not measure runtime quality or performance.

articles.name: Gomaa
articles.summary: Gomaa pairs a human-readable Obsidian Markdown vault with SQLite or PostgreSQL memory stores and exposes scoped retrieval through library, CLI, MCP, and adapter paths. This source review does not reproduce upstream performance claims or measure runtime quality.

articles.name: GoodAI LTM
articles.summary: GoodAI LTM is a Python library for text-based long-term memory and conversational agents. Its low-level memory stores a bounded stream of tokenized text chunks, indexes their embeddings, and retrieves relevant passages; optional models can rewrite queries or memories and rerank retrieved candidates. The repository also includes LTMAgent, which layers dialog and knowledge-base behavior over the memory library.

articles.name: GoodMemory
articles.summary: GoodMemory is a TypeScript memory library whose scoped remember, recall, context assembly, correction, and deletion flows are backed by storage adapters. Bun defaults to durable SQLite, while Node without a configured durable adapter falls back to in-memory storage.

articles.name: Google ADK
articles.summary: Google ADK’s Python package defines a memory service interface and three backends: an in-process event store, Vertex AI Memory Bank, and Vertex AI RAG. The durable backends delegate generation or retrieval to managed Google services; behavior such as deletion and provenance differs by backend. No runtime or benchmark was executed.

articles.name: Gortex
articles.summary: Gortex indexes tracked code repositories into a durable SQLite knowledge graph and exposes source-grounded code search and graph queries through CLI, MCP, HTTP, and a daemon. Its documentation also describes project documents and agent-session memories; this source review does not assess every memory lifecycle or measure runtime quality.

articles.name: Graft
articles.summary: Graft is a local-first coding-agent memory system built around a CLI and a long-lived daemon. It stores titled memory nodes, vectors, full-text indexes, graph edges, and source provenance in a per-profile SQLite database. Retrieval offers a gated single-answer query, hybrid ranked recall, and graph exploration; no Graft workload was run for this review.

articles.name: Graphicle
articles.summary: Graphicle is a local Rust application that combines a code graph, project documents and sessions, reviewed memory, MCP tools, a CLI, and a browser app. Agent-proposed memories remain drafts until approval; retrieval can return source excerpts and reviewed memories with citations. This is a source review, not a runtime evaluation.

articles.name: Graphify
articles.summary: Graphify is a local-first codebase knowledge graph and agent context tool. It builds a persistent graph from source, documents and media, then exposes graph queries through a CLI or MCP. A separate work-memory path stores Q&A records and derives a lessons artifact from recorded outcomes; this review describes source behavior and does not establish runtime quality or performance.

articles.name: Graphiti
articles.summary: Graphiti is an open-source Python framework that turns source episodes into a temporal knowledge graph of entities and relationship facts. It keeps episode provenance and supports hybrid graph retrieval; the library supplies graph construction, while a host application must provide production authentication, authorization, and tenant controls. This source review does not measure runtime quality or performance.

articles.name: GraQle
articles.summary: GraQle is a Python knowledge-graph and agent reasoning framework. Its durable project graph and separate in-process reasoning-round memory have distinct storage and scope models. This review is based on pinned public source and documentation; no runtime or benchmark result is claimed.

articles.name: GrayMatter
articles.summary: GrayMatter is a local-first Go memory store and MCP server for agent facts, with hybrid retrieval, revision/tombstone handling, optional citation and subject-aware tools, and optional knowledge-graph extraction. This review is pinned to current upstream source and does not measure runtime quality or performance.

articles.name: Grok Build
articles.summary: Grok Build is a Rust coding-agent CLI/TUI with cross-session memory. The inspected head contains two isolated pipelines: legacy Markdown notes and session logs with a SQLite hybrid-search index, and an opt-in v2 topic/observation pipeline with scoped access, durable capture, Dream consolidation, a generated manifest, and tombstone-based forgetting. Memory is experimental and disabled by default in the user guide. No runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run.

articles.name: growmos
articles.summary: Growmos is a repository-local knowledge graph for agent memory. It stores typed entities, relations, and provenance in editable JSONL, stages extraction and resolution through agent task packets, and retrieves bounded k-hop graph context with edge citations. This source review does not measure runtime quality or performance.

articles.name: GURU
articles.summary: GURU is an Android agent application whose Cerebrum memory engine is a Rust workspace hosted in-process by the app. The reviewed source describes layered buffer, episodic, and semantic memory, graph and lexical retrieval, event records, and an encrypted local vault. This is a source-based review; no app, tests, or benchmark was run.

articles.name: Habitus AI
articles.summary: Habitus AI is a Python agent-memory library that stores immutable event records in SQLite and routes retrieval and outcome learning through directional concept graphs. Its code describes direct dense plus graph-vault retrieval, correction by supersession, and receipt-gated graph reinforcement; this review reports code behavior and does not measure quality or performance.

articles.name: Halofy
articles.summary: Halofy is a self-hostable TypeScript kernel for governed organizational memory. It owns identity, policy, writes, audit, and erasure while delegating retrieval ranking to replaceable drivers. Postgres/pgvector is authoritative, with embedded PGlite as a local default; performance and answer quality were not measured.

articles.name: Harness Evolution as Learning
articles.summary: Harness Evolution as Learning is a research experiment repository for AppWorld agents. It compares prompt memory with learned checkers, statistics, action controls, and several memory-update algorithms. Its memory state is primarily maintained in process during an experiment and saved in run outputs; this review does not establish runtime quality or performance.

articles.name: Harness²
articles.summary: Harness² is a Python framework for recursively improving agent harnesses. Its filesystem experience library retains adopted harness trees and evidence-backed lessons per benchmark domain, run and mode. This source review does not execute the system or measure quality.

articles.name: Hatchdoor
articles.summary: Hatchdoor is a self-hosted Markdown vault server with browser and MCP interfaces. Markdown files are canonical and a disposable SQLite cache supports browsing, links, metadata, keyword search, and semantic search. The review describes inspected source mechanisms; no runtime quality or benchmark result was measured.

articles.name: Hats
articles.summary: Hats is a local agent runtime with workspace-scoped memory layers: user-authored context, a bounded inferred persona, short run takeaways, and operational lessons. Source review describes their file-backed lifecycle and retrieval behavior; it does not establish measured memory quality or isolation.

articles.name: Headroom
articles.summary: Headroom is a local-first LLM context compression library, proxy, and agent integration suite. Its optional persistent-memory subsystem adds hierarchical user/session/agent/turn memories, embedding and text retrieval, and project-aware storage. This review describes selected source and documentation, not runtime quality or performance.

articles.name: Heimdall
articles.summary: Heimdall is a local agent-memory and code-knowledge system that indexes files into graph and semantic search layers and verifies returned paths against filesystem evidence. The review is pinned to current upstream source and does not measure runtime quality or performance.

articles.name: Helix AGI
articles.summary: Helix AGI is a locally operated, persistent agent runtime that combines a filesystem home and ongoing sense/thinking/action loop with several memory stores. At the reviewed head, canonical journal records are append-only JSONL, categorized beliefs are JSON files, and semantic recall uses a separate vector index; retrieval/context assembly combines these distinct surfaces. This is a source review, not a runtime quality assessment.

articles.name: Helm
articles.summary: Helm is a self-hosted personal agent with structured memory in a local SQLite database. Its facts and conversation episodes are written through a CLI and tool wrappers, recalled using BM25 fused with TF-IDF cosine or cached local MiniLM embeddings, and maintained through periodic reflection and consolidation. This is a source review, not a runtime or benchmark result.

articles.name: Hermes Agent
articles.summary: Hermes Agent combines small, bounded profile memory files that are injected at session start with searchable conversation history stored in SQLite. The memory tool supports adding, patching, removing, and batched writes; session_search retrieves actual prior messages through FTS5. This review describes current documentation and selected source, not measured memory quality or performance.

articles.name: Hermes Fleet Memory
articles.summary: A self-operated MCP memory server that embeds cards and stores them in a shared Qdrant collection, with on-demand retrieval and client-configured domain gates. This is a source review; runtime quality and performance were not measured.

articles.name: Hermes Memory Installer
articles.summary: An agent-agnostic memory sidecar that indexes agent sessions, Hindsight facts and curated knowledge, archives sessions to gbrain, and generates fused recall context. This review records source observations, not measured quality or performance.

articles.name: Hestia
articles.summary: Hestia is a local-first household assistant with two distinct memory paths: Markdown soft facts/preferences and structured SQLite entities/events. Its conversational memory supports direct writes and lexical recall; background extraction proposes facts for human approval. This is a pinned source review, not a runtime or benchmark evaluation.

articles.name: HeurChain
articles.summary: HeurChain is a self-hosted Go memory broker that stores tenant-scoped agent memories in Redis and combines BM25 keyword search with dense Qdrant search. It supports sessions, lifecycle consolidation, versioned correction, and explicit forget operations. This review is source-based; no HeurChain runtime or project benchmark was run.

articles.name: Hexis
articles.summary: Hexis is a PostgreSQL centered cognitive architecture for a persistent agent. Its database stores memory, graph, belief/evidence, identity, and runtime state; PostgreSQL extensions provide vector and graph capabilities, while Python services expose database functions to chat, workers, CLI, and MCP paths. This review describes inspected source, not measured runtime quality.

articles.name: Hillock
articles.summary: Hillock is a local neuro-symbolic memory engine combining a SQLite fact graph, Hebbian associations, and hyperdimensional retrieval gating. This source-based review does not claim runtime or benchmark results.

articles.name: Hindsight
articles.summary: Hindsight is a service and SDK for agent memory that retains inputs into isolated banks, recalls them with semantic, keyword, graph, and temporal retrieval, and can derive evidence-backed observations and mental models. This source review does not measure runtime quality or performance.

articles.name: Hipocampus
articles.summary: Hipocampus is a project-local memory harness built around Markdown files, lifecycle hooks and agent skills. It keeps a compact topic index available at session start and combines a hierarchical compaction tree with optional qmd search. This source review does not reproduce upstream benchmark claims or measure runtime quality.

articles.name: Hippo
articles.summary: Hippo is a local-first memory system for coding agents, with a SQLite store, CLI/API/MCP integrations, tenant and project boundaries, lexical and optional vector retrieval, and lifecycle operations for superseding, forgetting, and maintaining memories. This review describes the current source at the verified upstream head; it is not a runtime or benchmark result.

articles.name: HippoRAG
articles.summary: HippoRAG is a Python framework for indexing documents into passage, entity, and fact embeddings plus a knowledge graph, then retrieving passages through fact scoring and graph propagation with dense-retrieval fallback. It also exposes persistent indexes through MCP. This source review does not measure runtime quality or performance.

articles.name: Hivemind
articles.summary: Hivemind is a local, single-user memory daemon for harnesses. It exposes MCP write and query tools backed by SQLite structured records and sqlite-vec; its default hash embedding is explicitly non-semantic, so semantic retrieval quality is not established by this review.

articles.name: Hivemind (Activeloop)
articles.summary: Hivemind is a multi-agent memory and trace-sharing system built around Activeloop Deeplake workspaces. It captures structured agent events, creates session summaries, mines reusable skills, and exposes the data through a virtual filesystem and retrieval hooks. This assessment describes pinned public source and documentation; it does not establish runtime quality or isolation.

articles.name: Hivemind (Lesur)
articles.summary: Hivemind is a self-hosted MCP service that organizes agent memory into short-lived notes, an editable Markdown project bank, and a derived graph/vector index. The tiers have different write and authority rules: SHORT captures activity, MID is the project handbook, and LONG helps discover related historical context but is non-authoritative. This review is source-based; no runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run.

articles.name: HiveMind (projectmentor)
articles.summary: HiveMind is a self-hosted peer-to-peer memory system whose append-only signed journal is replicated among devices and indexed locally by SQLite/FTS5. Confidence is projected from independent corroboration and owner governance. Its shared-hive access model and persistent journal history are material boundaries; benchmark behavior was not measured.

articles.name: HOLO-Invariant
articles.summary: HOLO-Invariant is a Python continuity framework whose core memory path is a local append-only, hash-linked JSONL chain with replay and search. Separate receipts represent corrections, and a service facade gates appends with target-bound authorization. This is a source review, not a runtime or benchmark result.

articles.name: Holographic
articles.summary: Holographic is a local SQLite memory provider for Hermes Agent. It stores versioned facts and entity links, and combines multilingual full-text matching, entity-aware recall, trust weighting, and optional holographic vector similarity. This review describes current source behavior; no runtime quality or performance was measured.

articles.name: holomem
articles.summary: HoloMem is a NumPy library that stores relational facts in memory and builds weighted FHRR traces for current, inverse, gated, and month-specific retrieval. It has no persistence or built-in scope boundary; this source review does not reproduce upstream benchmark claims.

articles.name: HomeBody
articles.summary: HomeBody is a humanoid robotics system whose persistent memory stores named, map-bound photographs with spatial pose and optional depth. It recalls historical views by nearby viewpoint rather than searching description text.

articles.name: Honcho
articles.summary: Honcho is a memory service and library for stateful agents. It stores peer-attributed messages in sessions, processes them asynchronously into conclusions and representations, and exposes semantic search, context and chat APIs. Workspaces, tenants and named scopes define important data boundaries; runtime benchmark behavior was not measured.

articles.name: Huiran-cerebro
articles.summary: Huiran-cerebro is a local-first Python memory and knowledge system built around SQLite, with Chinese-friendly FTS5, local embeddings, hybrid retrieval, a CLI, web UI, and MCP server. Its current code includes fragment lifecycle review and tombstones, mutation/retrieval audit tables, and namespace-aware paths. This assessment is a source review; no runtime or benchmark result is claimed.
